stem: Rina can encode one batch of forms in 4 hours. What part of the batch can she encode in 3 hours?
hints: If a job takes 4 hours, how much of it is done in 1 hour?
Her rate is 1/4 of the batch per hour.
Work done = rate × time. Multiply 1/4 by 3 hours.

solution.methodName: Work rates: rate = 1 ÷ time, then add the rates

steps.action: Let x = the part of the batch Rina encodes in 3 hours.
Her rate: 1 batch ÷ 4 hours = 1/4 of the batch per hour.
steps.why: A rate is how much of the job gets done in one hour.
Multiply the top number: 1 × 3 = 3. The bottom stays 4.

steps.action: Check: 3/4 is less than one whole batch, which makes sense because 3 hours is less than 4 hours. She encodes 3/4 of the batch.

trapNotes.1/4: This is what she does in 1 hour. Multiply by 3 for 3 hours.
trapNotes.4/3: This is the fraction upside down (4 ÷ 3). She cannot finish more than the whole batch in less than 4 hours.
trapNotes.1/12: This is 1 ÷ (4 × 3). Work done = rate × time, so multiply 1/4 by 3.
